This role is well suited for an experienced individual who enjoys solving complex engineering problems, developing practical AI solutions, and helping build a strong, collaborative technical team.

The successful candidate will bring strong expertise in AI/ML, industrial applications, and applied research. Depending on their background, they may contribute primarily to one or more of the following areas:

Predictive Maintenance, Condition-Based Maintenance, and Prognostics and Health Management (PHM).

  • Oil and Gas, including petroleum engineering, drilling, production, and related engineering research.

  • Generative AI applications, including enterprise AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), intelligent engineering tools, and cloud-based AI solutions.

This role requires the ability to translate research and emerging technologies into scalable, production-ready solutions that improve operational performance, engineering decision-making, asset reliability, and business outcomes.

  • Serve as a technical expert in Industrial AI, providing leadership and consulting support to NOV business units and engineering teams.
  • Identify high-value industrial and engineering use cases for artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced analytics.
  • Design, develop, validate, deploy, and monitor production-ready AI/ML solutions.
  • Lead the full data science and AI lifecycle, including problem definition, data exploration, feature engineering, model development, validation, deployment, and performance monitoring.

  • Develop solutions in one or more focus areas:

    • Predictive maintenance, equipment health monitoring, anomaly detection, fault diagnosis, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, and maintenance optimization

    • Oil and gas applications, including drilling analytics, well and reservoir-related workflows, production optimization, and petroleum engineering research

    • Generative AI, LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), intelligent agents, document intelligence, and AI-assisted engineering applications

  • Apply advanced methods in machine learning, deep learning, time-series modeling, computer vision, natural language processing, Generative AI, and LLMs.
  • Collaborate with petroleum engineers, mechanical engineers, software developers, product teams, data engineers, and subject matter experts to convert business needs into practical AI solutions.
  • Design scalable data and analytics pipelines and contribute to cloud-based AI and MLOps platforms.
  • Evaluate emerging AI technologies, conduct applied research, and translate research outcomes into industrial solutions.
  • Communicate technical findings, recommendations, and project outcomes to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Contribute to technical documentation, publications, patents, invention disclosures, and innovation initiatives.
  • Support the expansion of NOV’s data science capabilities in India by sharing knowledge, establishing best practices, and contributing to team development.
  • Take on increasing leadership responsibilities, with the opportunity to lead and mentor the India-based data science team in the coming year.
  • Mentor junior team members and promote best practices in AI, machine learning, software engineering, and responsible technology adoption.

We are looking for a motivated and technically strong professional who can work independently and collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and apply advanced AI methods to real-world industrial problems. The ideal candidate will also be interested in helping build and lead a growing data science organization.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Petroleum Engineering, or a related STEM discipline, with 10 or more years of relevant industrial experience.
• Master’s degree in a relevant discipline with 8 or more years of relevant industrial experience is preferred.
• Ph.D. in a relevant discipline with 7 or more years of industrial experience is preferred.
• Relevant industrial experience may include work in Industrial AI, data science, machine learning, petroleum engineering, drilling research, engineering analytics, software engineering, or related fields.
• Demonstrated ability to deliver AI/ML solutions from research or concept through production deployment.
• Experience mentoring, guiding, or technically leading data scientists or multidisciplinary engineering teams is preferred.
• Strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, statistical modeling, optimization, and predictive analytics.
• Experience with one or more of the following:
o Time-series analysis, anomaly detection, fault diagnosis, and failure prediction
o Computer vision and image or video analytics
o Natural language processing and information retrieval
o Generative AI, LLMs, RAG, prompt engineering, and AI agents.

title: Aftermarket Technician
description:
About the Role

As an Aftermarket Technician, you will perform the assembly, disassembly, servicing, inspection, repair, and pressure testing of Pressure Control Equipment (PCE), including hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Working within the Aftermarket Service & Rental team, you will contribute to delivering safe, reliable, and high-quality equipment while supporting operational excellence and continuous improvement.

This is a hands-on technical position requiring strong mechanical aptitude, problem-solving skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a workshop environment.

About the Team

You will join a close-knit team of experienced technicians working alongside the wider Service Department at our Kintore facility. The team values collaboration, knowledge sharing, reliability, and personal accountability while encouraging technicians to take ownership of their work.

Why This Role Matters

Your work directly supports the reliability and safety of equipment used in well intervention operations. By ensuring equipment is serviced, tested, and repaired to the highest standards, you will help maintain operational performance, product quality, and customer confidence.

About NOV

NOV's Intervention & Stimulation Equipment business delivers industry-leading pressure control technologies and aftermarket services supporting well intervention and production operations worldwide. Through engineering expertise, manufacturing excellence, and lifecycle support, NOV helps customers improve safety, operational reliability, and equipment performance across global energy markets.

What We Offer

At NOV, you'll join an experienced technical team within a modern workshop environment where continuous learning and practical development are encouraged. You'll receive structured on-the-job training, opportunities to develop specialist technical skills, and exposure to industry-leading pressure control equipment. We foster a collaborative culture where safety, quality, teamwork, and continuous improvement are at the heart of everything we do.

Diversity & Inclusion

At NOV, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We value diversity in all its forms and believe that different perspectives drive innovation and success. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, nationality, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

  • Assemble, disassemble, service, inspect, repair, and test Pressure Control Equipment (PCE).
  • Diagnose faults and troubleshoot hydraulic and pneumatic systems.
  • Perform pressure testing in accordance with approved procedures and quality standards.
  • Interpret engineering drawings, technical documentation, and work instructions to complete assigned tasks accurately.
  • Maintain high standards of quality, housekeeping, and workplace safety within the workshop.
  • Identify equipment issues and report opportunities for product or process improvements.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives, including Lean and 5S activities.
  • Work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative workshop team.
  • Participate in daily team meetings and contribute to operational planning.
  • Support colleagues across the workshop when required to achieve business objectives.
  • Complete work safely, efficiently, and in compliance with NOV policies and procedures.
  • Be prepared to work reasonable overtime when operational requirements demand.

Essential Qualifications

Experience

  • Experience within a mechanical maintenance, manufacturing, service, or workshop environment.
  • Practical experience working with mechanical equipment.
  • Experience working with hydraulic and/or pneumatic systems.
  • Ability to diagnose technical faults and solve mechanical problems.

Technical Skills

  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation.
  • Ability to safely operate standard hand and power tools.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently using sound judgement and initiative.

Personal Attributes

  • Reliable with a strong commitment to attendance and safety.
  • Strong attention to detail and quality.
  • Team player who is equally comfortable working independently.
  • Positive attitude with a willingness to learn new skills and processes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Time-served apprenticeship or equivalent mechanical trade qualification.
  • NC qualification or equivalent in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Experience servicing or repairing Pressure Control Equipment (PCE).
  • Experience working with Wireline or Well Intervention equipment.
  • Experience carrying out pressure testing activities.
  • Forklift certificate.
  • Overhead crane certificate.
  • Knowledge of Elmar or Anson product lines.
  • Previous experience within the energy, oil & gas, industrial equipment, or heavy engineering sectors.

title: QC Engineer
description:
As QC Engineer, you will join the Supply Chain team and help ensure that equipment and materials delivered by suppliers meet project, contractual, quality and applicable regulatory requirements. The role combines engineering understanding with practical supplier-quality coordination and inspection activities.

You will work across different project packages, including areas such as jacking systems, cranes and aftermarket activities. During your first months, you will become familiar with GustoMSC projects, products and processes from end to end, before taking on greater technical responsibility and independent ownership.

The position is based in Schiedam, Netherlands, with regular office presence and international travel. Travel is mainly within Europe and typically involves short trips of one or two days, although assignments of up to approximately one week and occasional travel outside Europe may be required.

  • Perform and support supplier inspections, Factory Acceptance Tests (FATs), kick-off meetings and quality audits.
  • Review and coordinate supplier quality documentation and verify compliance with contracts, purchase orders, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and technical specifications.
  • Identify, initiate and follow through on Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), punch-list items and technical queries until closure.
  • Prepare clear and accurate inspection and supplier-visit reports and follow up on agreed corrective actions.
  • Coordinate quality activities and technical interfaces with suppliers, engineering teams, project stakeholders and other relevant parties.
  • Apply your understanding of materials, welding, structures and fabrication to identify and resolve quality issues.
  • Contribute to project packages as a Package Engineer and, as experience develops, potentially take broader Package Manager responsibilities.
  • Support continuous improvement of quality methods, standards and working practices while following NOV HSE requirements.

Must-Have

  • Relevant engineering background, particularly in mechanical engineering, materials or a comparable technical discipline.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or an equivalent level of capability gained through relevant experience.
  • Practical understanding of materials, welding and structural/fabrication principles.
  • Relevant professional experience sufficient to work independently in an engineering or quality environment; this is intended as a mid-level rather than graduate position.
  • Ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with suppliers and internal technical stakeholders.
  • Strong written and spoken English, including the ability to produce clear technical and inspection reports.
  • Proactive and independent approach to identifying and resolving quality issues within established processes.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake international business travel, primarily within Europe.
  • Driving licence. ,

Preferred

  • Previous QA/QC, supplier quality, equipment verification or vendor quality management experience.
  • Experience within offshore, marine or another relevant engineered-equipment/fabrication environment.
  • Knowledge of relevant engineering rules, regulations and quality standards.
  • Experience with fabrication workflows, inspection planning and/or document-control systems.
  • Dutch language capability for communication with local suppliers.
  • VCA VOL certification.

What we offer

  • A 12-month assignment with the possibility of extension and potential longer-term opportunities.
  • Exposure to varied international projects and engineered equipment, including jacking systems, cranes and aftermarket activities.
  • International supplier and inspection exposure, primarily across Europe.
  • Opportunity to develop deeper technical expertise and progressively take on greater responsibility.
  • Hybrid working arrangement: four days in the Schiedam office and one day from home.

From managing your team and overseeing daily operations to analyzing sales and planning promotions, your leadership shapes what customers find and feel every time they visit the deli.

Your Skills

  • Deliver outstanding customer service and inspire your team to do the same

  • Lead, motivate, and develop a team in a fast-paced food service environment

  • Solve practical problems and make sound decisions with a variety of variables

title: Manager, Enterprise Architecture
description:
At Children’s Wisconsin, we believe kids deserve the best.

Children’s Wisconsin is a nationally recognized health system dedicated solely to the health and well-being of children. We provide primary care, specialty care, urgent care, emergency care, community health services, foster and adoption services, child and family counseling, child advocacy services and family resource centers. Our reputation draws patients and families from around the country.

We offer a wide variety of rewarding career opportunities and are seeking individuals dedicated to helping us achieve our vision of the healthiest kids in the country. If you want to work for an organization that makes a difference for children and families, and encourages you to be at your best every day, please apply today.

Please follow this link for a closer look at what it’s like to work at Children’s Wisconsin:

**This is a full time, salaried, hybrid position based out of Milwaukee, Wisconsin.


Job Summary
This job will connect Children's Wisconsin's clinical and business priorities to practical technology direction and solution designs. Personally develop enterprise roadmaps and standards, architect complex solutions with particular depth in infrastructure, and establish and lead the architecture practice. The role will improve technology investment decisions, reduce unnecessary complexity and risk, and guide delivery of secure, reliable, and supportable services. The position combines principal architect responsibilities with management of a developing enterprise architecture function. Initially performs the architecture work directly, establishing the methods, relationships, and reusable designs needed to support delivery; continues substantial individual architecture work as the team grows. Scope spans business capabilities, applications, data and integration, infrastructure, and cloud, with domain specialists contributing detailed expertise. Partners with the CISO's organization, which retains security architecture and security policy ownership.

Essential Functions

  • Enterprise direction and roadmaps. Translates organizational strategy and clinical and business needs into current state assessments, target architectures, and achievable transition roadmaps. Connects business capabilities to applications, data, platforms, and services. Identifies dependencies, duplication, technical debt, and lifecycle risks and recommends sequenced improvements aligned with available funding and delivery capacity.
  • Solution architecture. Personally leads architecture for complex initiatives from discovery through implementation. Defines requirements, integration points, system boundaries, and quality expectations for availability, performance, security, recovery, and support. Produces solution diagrams, options analyses, design decisions, and implementation guidance. Resolves cross domain tradeoffs and validates that delivered solutions meet the approved design intent.
  • Infrastructure and cloud architecture. Provides deep architecture expertise across enterprise networks, compute, virtualization, storage, identity dependencies, resilience, and hybrid cloud. Develops reference architectures and evaluates hosting and modernization options. Works with Cloud Engineering on Azure foundations supporting analytics and later cloud expansion, and with Infrastructure on workload placement and phased data center migration designs.
  • Architecture governance and standards. Establishes practical architecture principles, standards, review criteria, and decision records. Leads reviews early enough to influence design and purchasing decisions. Documents exceptions, owners, risks, and remediation plans; escalates unresolved decisions through approved governance. Scales review effort to impact and risk and tracks decisions through delivery.
  • Investment and technology evaluation. Evaluates proposed technologies and vendor solutions for enterprise fit, integration, operating cost, lifecycle, and supportability. Develops recommendations with service owners, the IT Business Office, and procurement. Provides architecture input to investment prioritization and sourcing decisions and identifies opportunities to reuse platforms or retire redundant technology.
  • Architecture practice development. Builds and maintains a usable architecture repository, including standards, reference designs, roadmaps, and decision records. Establishes a repeatable engagement model with project and service teams. Coordinates application portfolio and dependency information with designated record owners and connects architecture priorities to enterprise planning and delivery.
  • People and practice leadership. Plans architecture workload and staffing, recruits the additional architect as approved, and establishes goals and development plans. Coaches staff, evaluates performance, and addresses performance needs as the team grows. Mentors technical leads across IS and builds shared architecture skills without creating dependence on a single decision maker.
  • Delivery partnership. Works directly with engineers, application owners, analytics teams, and vendors to test assumptions, assess feasibility, and resolve design issues. Participates in proofs of concept and reviews technical deliverables. Provides architecture guidance through implementation and operational handoff; engineering teams retain build and operational accountability.
  • Communication and accountability. Explains technology choices, costs, dependencies, and risks to clinical, business, and technology leaders. Facilitates decisions across teams with competing priorities. Reports roadmap progress, material exceptions, and architecture outcomes to the CTO and governance groups and adjusts priorities as organizational needs change.


Education

  • Bachelor's Degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, business, or a related field required
  • or relevant experience


Experience

  • 7+ years of progressively responsible technology experience, including substantial responsibility for enterprise architecture, solution architecture, and infrastructure design in a complex organization. Demonstrated experience personally producing architecture deliverables and guiding solutions through implementation. required
  • 7+ years enterprise architecture. Experience developing current and target state architectures, technology standards, and transition roadmaps tied to business needs. required
  • 7+ years solution and infrastructure architecture. Strong infrastructure architecture depth, supported by prior engineering or implementation experience. Experience defining requirements, evaluating options, documenting design tradeoffs, and guiding integrated solutions into operation. required
  • 5+ years leadership and execution. Experience leading architecture decisions across teams, facilitating stakeholder agreement, and mentoring technical professionals. required
  • 5+ years experience establishing an enterprise architecture practice; recruiting or managing architects; or leading architecture in healthcare or another environment requiring continuous service availability. Azure solution architecture, AWS, analytics platform enablement, application rationalization, and data center migration experience are preferred. Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks and modeling methods, and relevant enterprise or cloud architecture certifications, are preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Demonstrated ability to connect business capabilities, applications, data, integration and infrastructure; evaluate portfolio and lifecycle implications; and apply architecture governance to real investment and deliver decisions.
  • Proven ability to work independently as the initial architect, prioritize competing demands, establish practical methods and communicate recommendations to executive and technical audiences.
  • Ability to assume formal people management responsibilities as staffing grows.
  • Demonstrated ability to design across network, compute, storage, identity, resilience and cloud dependencies using domain specialists where needed.

title: Intern
description:
The intern will assist experienced technicians, the Workshop Supervisor, Repair Manager, and Project Managers in daily repair activities, technical documentation flow, reporting, and final documentation compilation. The position does not independently approve work, release documentation, or perform unsupervised critical activities.

Safety, HSEQ, and Compliance

  • Treat health, safety, environmental compliance, and product quality as first priorities in all workshop and documentation activities.

  • Work in accordance with NOV policies, procedures, the NOV Code of Business Conduct and Ethical Standards, and applicable local statutory rules and regulations.

  • Follow relevant Management System requirements, work instructions, inspection criteria, and equipment operation guidelines.

  • Participate in toolbox talks, daily team meetings, and safety discussions; raise concerns promptly and stop work when a potentially hazardous situation is identified.

  • Report non-conformities, undesired events, defects, discrepancies, and unsafe conditions according to existing quality and HSEQ procedures.

2. Mechanical Repair and Workshop Support

  • Assist experienced technicians with assembly, fitting, disassembly, inspection, rework, and repair of equipment within the NOV Rig product line.

  • Learn to read and interpret basic blueprints, diagrams, engineering drawings, job routes, and assembly/repair procedures.

  • Support the inspection of materials, products, and equipment for defects using gauges, visual checks, and measuring tools under supervision.

  • Assist in reworking or repairing equipment in line with engineering changes, specifications, and approved instructions.

  • Help maintain production quality and quantity by following approved standards, procedures, route times, and work priorities.

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area and support 5S principles, inventory discipline, and tool control.

  • Support timely completion of required workshop procedures, checklists, inspection records, and repair paperwork.

  • Be open to travel and additional duties when required by the business and approved by the relevant supervisor.

3. Document Control and Project Documentation Support

  • Assist the Repair Management Team with controlled documentation for repair projects and related operational activities.

  • Register, track, and distribute incoming and outgoing technical documentation to and from clients, suppliers, third parties, and internal stakeholders according to procedures.

  • Create and follow workflows for internal and external review comments on technical documentation.

  • Support preparation of project-specific document control procedures and supplier document submission requirements, based on contractual and internal requirements.

  • Assist with importing and maintaining the Master Document Register (MDR) at project start-up based on input from Project Managers.

  • Compile, check, and organize final documentation packages according to external and internal requirements under Project Manager supervision.

  • Prepare document reports and help follow up project documentation progress, overdue actions, and submission status.

  • Participate in project meetings and kick-off meetings when required, capturing relevant documentation actions and follow-ups.

4. Quality, Continuous Improvement, and Problem Solving

  • Accurately describe and document findings during quality investigations to support root cause analysis and corrective actions.

  • Assist the Workshop Supervisor and Repair Management Team in identifying, documenting, and eliminating non-conformance issues.

  • Support proactive problem-solving using methods such as Fishbone diagrams and structured brainstorming.

  • Contribute ideas for improving assembly, repair, document flow, quality control, and on-time delivery performance.

  • Assist with implementation of new techniques, equipment, or process improvements as part of continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Strive to support key performance indicators related to safety, quality, cost, delivery, and documentation accuracy.

Education

  • Student in Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program, diploma, or vocational/technical education with relevant content in mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, maintenance, repair, quality, documentation, or a related discipline.

  • Relevant practical experience, technical training, or strong demonstrated aptitude may be considered as an alternative to the preferred educational background.

Experience

  • No previous document control or mechanical repair experience is required; this role is intended for learning and development.

  • Any exposure to workshops, mechanical repair, manufacturing, maintenance, quality control, engineering documentation, MS Office, or project administration is beneficial.

Skills and Competencies

  • Good working knowledge of MS Office and ability to learn document control systems, registers, and reporting tools.

  • Good written and oral English; ability to communicate clearly with supervisors, technicians, Project Managers, clients, suppliers, and third parties when required.

  • Technical aptitude and willingness to learn drawings, procedures, measuring tools, repair methods, and documentation standards.

  • Organized, punctual, detail-oriented, and able to maintain accurate records while supporting practical workshop tasks.

title: Senior Software Engineer - AI
description:
NOV Process & Flow Technologies AS is seeking a Senior Software Engineer specialized in Agentic AI to join the Global Engineering Disciplines team. Based flexibly near our Fornebu offices, you will report to the Director of Global Engineering Disciplines and drive the creation of intelligent autonomous agents that automate engineering, operational, and business workflows across our energy, industrial, and offshore solutions.
  • Design and implement autonomous AI agents capable of multi‑step reasoning, tool calling, workflow orchestration, and human‑in‑the‑loop decision support.
  • Develop scalable AI services using frameworks such as OpenAI APIs, LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and Semantic Kernel.
  • Build Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and vector‑database knowledge management solutions.
  • Integrate AI agents with enterprise applications, ERP/CRM systems, and process data platforms.
  • Create production‑grade software using Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, FastAPI, Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud‑native architectures.
  • Implement robust testing, monitoring, observability, and security practices for AI workloads.
  • Establish AI governance frameworks covering evaluation, safety controls, hallucination mitigation, and compliance.
  • Prototype emerging technologies in LLMs, reinforcement learning, knowledge graphs, and autonomous workflows.
  • Collaborate with process engineers, automation specialists, and business stakeholders to deliver measurable value.
  • Define reusable AI architecture standards and contribute to NOV’s strategic AI roadmap.
  • Develop non-AI related software making use of AI tools for development, testing, implementation, maintenance
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI, or related field.
  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • 2+ years developing AI/ML applications in production, including LLM‑powered solutions.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and modern software architecture/design patterns.
  • Hands‑on experience with OpenAI, Anthropic, or comparable LLM platforms.
  • Experience with agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, or CrewAI.
  • Proficiency in vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, Azure AI Search) and RAG systems.
  • Knowledge of cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP) and container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Experience integrating AI solutions into enterprise environments and building APIs/microservices.
  • Preferred: background in industrial, energy, offshore, or process‑systems domains and familiarity with digital twins or advanced analytics.

What we offer

  • The opportunity to shape and drive AI innovation across a global engineering organization.
  • Ownership of high-impact projects, with the autonomy to turn ideas into production solutions that deliver measurable business value.
  • A collaborative environment where new technologies are encouraged, tested, and rapidly adopted rather than constrained by lengthy development cycles.
  • The chance to work alongside experienced engineering, automation, and digital specialists while solving real-world challenges in the energy and industrial sectors.
  • Excellent opportunities for professional growth, technical leadership, and visibility across NOV as you help define the future of AI-enabled engineering.
  • A competitive compensation package, comprehensive benefits, and a supportive work environment focused on continuous learning and innovation.

title: Hy-Chi Clerk
location: Windsor Heights, University Ave, Windsor Heights, IA
description:

At Hy-Vee our people are our strength. We promise “a helpful smile in every aisle” and those smiles can only come from a workforce that is fully engaged and committed to supporting our customers and each other.

Job Description:

Job Title: Hy-Chi Department Clerk

Department: Hy-Chi

FLSA: Hourly

Revision Date: 07/2026

About Hy-Vee

At Hy-Vee, we believe the shortest distance between two people is a smile. We're seeking people with a passion for customer service, a willingness to learn, and a commitment to being part of a team that strives to make our customers' lives easier, healthier and happier.

The Role and Why It's Important

At Hy-Vee, our Hy-Chi department offers customers a unique and delicious experience, and our Hy-Chi Department Clerks are at the heart of making it happen. In this role, you'll fill customer orders, prepare and replenish product, keep the department running smoothly, and deliver the kind of friendly service that makes every customer feel welcome. Whether you're taking an order at the counter, pulling product from the cooler, or keeping the workspace clean and organized, your work makes a real difference every shift.

If you enjoy a fast-paced food service environment, take pride in quality, and love working with people, we'd love to have you on our team.

What You'll Do

No two shifts are exactly the same, but here's what you can expect:

  • Deliver outstanding customer service by greeting every customer with a smile, taking orders at the Hy-Chi counter, and assisting them with their needs throughout the store

  • Review orders for the day and ensure an adequate food supply is ready and on hand by developing or following a production list

  • Prepare, finish, and replenish product as necessary and pull product from the cooler or freezer to prepare for cooking

  • Review the status and appearance of food for freshness and maintain quality standards throughout the shift

  • Check in product, put product away, and review invoices as needed

  • Run the department register, receive payment, and make change as applicable

  • Practice proper sanitation procedures and keep the work area clean, neat, and safe at all times

  • Remove trash in a timely manner and wash dishes as necessary

  • Order product and supplies and price product for customers as needed

  • Answer the phone promptly and provide friendly, helpful service to customers who call, including taking customer orders

  • Follow Hy-Vee's dress code, hygiene standards, and all department and company guidelines

  • Pitch in with other tasks or special projects as they come up

Your Skills

You don't need extensive experience for this role; we'll provide the training you need to succeed. To hit the ground running, you'll need to be able to:

  • Bring commitment to Hy-Vee's mission and a genuine passion for helping customers

title: K9 Handler Security Patrol
description:
K9 Security Patrol Handler

Byers K9 Services | BKS Security

Byers K9 Services is seeking dependable, professional, and motivated individuals for the position of K9 Security Patrol Handler. This position combines traditional security responsibilities with the deployment, handling, care, and continued training of a company-owned working K9.

K9 Security Patrol Handlers are responsible for maintaining a visible security presence, conducting proactive patrols, identifying and reporting suspicious or unsafe activity, protecting client property, and properly deploying their assigned K9 when appropriate.

This is a working K9 position, not simply a security position with a dog. Handlers are expected to maintain a high standard of professionalism, physical capability, situational awareness, report writing, K9 control, and accountability both on and off duty.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Conduct routine and randomized foot patrols throughout assigned client properties.

  • Maintain a highly visible security and K9 presence to deter theft, trespassing, vandalism, and other criminal activity.

  • Inspect buildings, construction areas, gates, fencing, vehicles, equipment, and other designated areas.

  • Identify suspicious persons, vehicles, activities, safety hazards, and security concerns.

  • Professionally approach and address unauthorized individuals when appropriate.

  • Enforce client site rules and established post orders.

  • Contact law enforcement, fire, EMS, supervisors, or client representatives when circumstances require.

  • Complete accurate and detailed daily activity reports, patrol documentation, incident reports, and other required records.

  • Properly operate company-issued radios, body-worn cameras, mobile applications, and security equipment.

  • Maintain situational awareness and immediately report unusual or significant activity.

  • Remain awake, alert, attentive, and actively engaged for the entire assigned shift.

K9 Handler Responsibilities

Handlers may be partnered with a company-owned working K9 and are responsible for the professional handling and daily care of that K9 in accordance with BKS policies and training standards.

Responsibilities include:

  • Safely handle and maintain control of the assigned K9 at all times.

  • Deploy the K9 during security patrols as authorized by company policy and client requirements.

  • Conduct required maintenance training and participate in scheduled company K9 training.

  • Maintain proficiency in obedience, control, environmental exposure, patrol techniques, and other assigned disciplines.

  • Properly maintain K9 equipment including collars, leashes, harnesses, crates, training equipment, and related gear.

  • Maintain the K9's approved feeding, watering, exercise, grooming, and care schedule.

  • Monitor the K9 for injury, illness, behavioral changes, or other concerns and immediately report them.

  • Transport the K9 safely using an approved vehicle and secured K9 crate or containment system.

  • Maintain an appropriate home environment for the K9 when authorized for home housing.

  • Follow all company requirements concerning veterinary care, nutrition, medications, training tools, and K9 management.

All K9s assigned through this program remain the sole property of Byers K9 Services. Assignment of a K9 does not constitute ownership or create any ownership interest in the animal.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants must:

  • Be at least 18 years of age.

  • Possess a valid driver's license.

  • Have reliable transportation.

  • Be legally authorized to work in the United States.

  • Successfully complete all required background screening.

  • Meet any state or local licensing requirements applicable to the assignment.

  • Have the ability to stand and walk for extended periods.

  • Be capable of working outdoors in varying weather conditions.

  • Be physically capable of controlling a working German Shepherd, Belgian Malinois, Dutch Shepherd, or similar working breed.

  • Be comfortable working independently with limited direct supervision.

  • Possess strong communication and observational skills.

  • Be capable of writing clear and accurate reports.

  • Have a working smartphone and the ability to use company-required applications.

  • Maintain professional appearance and conduct.

K9-Specific Requirements

Candidates selected for the K9 program must be willing and able to:

  • Successfully complete the BKS-approved K9 Handler Academy and/or evaluation process before independent deployment.

  • Demonstrate safe and competent handling of a working K9.

  • Participate in continuing K9 training and proficiency evaluations.

  • Maintain the K9 according to company standards while the K9 is assigned to them.

  • Complete a home inspection before being approved to house a company K9.

  • Have a living arrangement that safely accommodates a working K9.

  • Maintain reliable transportation capable of safely transporting the K9 and required equipment.

  • Follow BKS policies regarding K9 handling both on and off duty.

Previous K9 handling experience is preferred but is not necessarily required for candidates selected for company-sponsored training.

Preferred Experience

Preference may be given to applicants with previous experience in:

  • Military or law enforcement

  • Security operations

  • Police or military working dogs

  • Private-sector K9 handling

  • Working-dog training

  • Patrol or detection K9 operations

  • Corrections

  • Emergency services

  • Construction-site security

  • High-value asset protection

Work Environment

This position may include:

  • Overnight shifts

  • Weekends and holidays

  • 8–12+ hour shifts

  • Extended periods of walking and standing

  • Exterior patrols

  • Construction sites

  • Commercial and residential developments

  • Industrial properties

  • Uneven terrain

  • Exposure to heat, cold, rain, snow, and other weather conditions

Handlers must be comfortable working independently during overnight hours and responding appropriately to potentially unpredictable situations.

Professional Standards

K9 Security Patrol Handlers represent both BKS Security and Byers K9 Services while assigned to a client property. Employees are expected to demonstrate professionalism, sound judgment, integrity, reliability, and appropriate conduct at all times.

Sleeping while on duty, abandoning an assigned post, falsifying patrol or training records, mistreating a K9, unauthorized use of a company K9, or other serious violations of company policy may result in immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination.

Equipment

Depending on assignment, employees may be issued company equipment including:

  • Uniform shirts and patches

  • K9 collars, leashes, and harnesses

  • Training equipment

  • K9 crate

  • Body-worn camera

  • Safety equipment

  • Other site- or K9-specific equipment

All issued equipment and K9 property remain the property of Byers K9 Services and must be properly maintained and returned when required.

Position Type

K9 Security Patrol Handler

Schedules and assignments vary according to client needs and may include nights, weekends, holidays, and extended shifts.

Byers K9 Services is looking for individuals who want to develop professionally as working K9 handlers, not simply employees looking for a security assignment. Successful candidates must be willing to train, accept coaching, maintain high performance standards, and take responsibility for both their assigned security duties and their K9 partner.

title: Global Finance Learning & Capability Development Lead
description:
The Global Finance Learning & Capability Development Lead owns the global learning and capability agenda that enables NOV Finance to perform effectively today and evolve for the future. As a trusted advisor to Finance leadership on organizational capability and workforce readiness, the role translates business and Finance priorities, technology evolution, transformation needs, and changes in the profession into practical, scalable development solutions that strengthen foundational, role-specific, and emerging capabilities.

This is a hands-on role responsible for both shaping and executing the Finance learning agenda, including learning architecture, curricula, content development, delivery, learning platforms, governance, and measurement. The role also supports career and talent development as part of building Finance capability and strengthening the future talent pipeline.

The role works across Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology, transformation teams, and subject-matter experts to deliver relevant, scalable solutions that meet the needs of a diverse global Finance organization.

Finance Capability, Acumen & Future Skills

  • Own an enterprise-wide view of the capabilities required across NOV Finance, partnering with Finance leaders and subject-matter experts to define foundational Finance and business acumen, functional expertise, technology fluency, digital and data skills, AI-enabled ways of working, and leadership capabilities.
  • Establish and maintain the global Finance core curriculum, capability models, and role-based competency frameworks, and assess gaps to guide learning, upskilling, reskilling, and workforce development priorities.
  • Anticipate how Finance capability requirements are evolving, monitoring changes in NOV's business, operating model, technology, regulatory environment, and the Finance profession and translating them into future capability priorities.

Learning Strategy, Development & Delivery

  • Translate Finance capability priorities into a scalable global learning agenda, including curricula and role-based learning journeys for onboarding, foundational development, upskilling, reskilling, leadership development, and career progression.
  • Manage Finance learning and capability initiatives as disciplined global programs, with clear priorities, milestones, ownership, governance, and accountability for execution
  • Design and deliver practical learning solutions, personally developing content and facilitating programs where appropriate while partnering with subject-matter experts and using formal learning, digital content, mentoring, peer learning, and on-the-job development.
  • Own the Finance learning portfolio, platforms, and external partnerships, ensuring effective governance, delivery, tracking, reporting, and content maintenance while leveraging external providers, professional organizations, universities, and certifications where they add value.

Career, Talent & Leadership

  • Build Finance career pathways, mobility, rotations, and development experiences that help employees understand career opportunities, build critical capabilities, and prepare for future roles.

  • Coordinate Finance talent and succession processes, strengthening pipelines for critical roles and ensuring high-potential and critical talent receive deliberate development through learning, mentoring, rotations, special projects, and other experiences.

  • Develop Finance managers and future leaders, building capabilities in coaching, feedback, performance management, business acumen, enterprise thinking, leading change, influence, and talent development.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Measure and report Finance capability development and workforce readiness, including learning effectiveness, skill development, application on the job, talent pipelines, mobility, and succession depth.
  • Evaluate success based on improvements in capability and employee effectiveness—not simply participation and completion—and provide leaders with actionable insight into progress and gaps.
  • Use data, employee and leader feedback, and external practices to continuously improve the Finance learning and capability agenda.

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Human Resources, Organizational Development, Learning & Development, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certification is a plus.

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in learning and development, organizational capability, talent development, Finance transformation, Finance operations, or related areas, ideally supporting a Finance or Accounting organization in a complex global environment.

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience designing, building, and delivering learning programs, including translating capability needs into curricula and development solutions, developing content with subject-matter experts, and administering enterprise learning platforms.

  • Strong Finance and Accounting acumen with the credibility to engage Finance leaders, understand functional and emerging capability needs, and translate complex Finance topics into effective development solutions. Finance, Finance transformation, or Finance capability-development experience is strongly preferred.

  • Strong program management and execution skills, with the ability to move between strategy and hands-on delivery and take initiatives from concept through implementation and sustainable operation.

  • Strong communication, facilitation, stakeholder-management, and digital skills, including comfort with learning technologies, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled tools.

  • Curious, adaptable, and development-oriented, with the ability to anticipate how Finance and its capability requirements are evolving, influence across a matrixed global organization, and help people build skills and advance their careers.

title: Full Time Key Carrier
description:
Marshalls

At TJX Companies, every day brings new opportunities for growth, exploration, and achievement. You’ll be part of our vibrant team that embraces diversity, fosters collaboration, and prioritizes your development. Whether you’re working in our four global Home Offices, Distribution Centers or Retail Stores—TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Homegoods, Homesense, Sierra, Winners, and TK Maxx, you’ll find abundant opportunities to learn, thrive, and make an impact. Come join our TJX family—a Fortune 100 company and the world’s leading off-price retailer.

Job Description:

Opportunity: Grow Your Career

The Key Carrier role is an elevated extension of the Coordinator role. Key Carriers alternate their role based on store needs, predominantly performing the role of Coordinator and occasionally acting as Key Carrier, taking on a leadership role in maintaining all aspects of the store. Key Carriers must have open availability, including nights and weekends. Role models exceptional customer service.

  • Creates a positive internal and external customer experience
  • Promotes a culture of honesty and integrity; maintains confidentiality
  • Acts as Manager on Duty adhering to company policy and procedure
  • Ensures store team performs tasks and activities in accordance with store plan; prioritizes as needed
  • Addresses immediate customer service issues and provides appropriate coaching to Associates
  • Exercises discretion regarding customer service policies to satisfy customers
  • Maintains accurate Associate coverage in service areas for a positive customer experience
  • Ensures Associates adhere to all operational procedures
  • Ensures opening/closing procedures are executed according to company guidelines
  • Communicates accurately and effectively with management and Associates when setting and addressing priorities; provides progress updates
  • Provides and accepts recognition and constructive feedback
  • Provides feedback, recognition and coaching to Associates
  • Partners with Management on Associate training needs to increase effectiveness
  • Ensures adherence to all labor laws, policies, and procedures
  • Promotes credit and loyalty programs
  • Supports and participates in shrink reduction goals and programs
  • Promotes safety awareness and maintains a safe environment
  • Other duties as assigned

Who We’re Looking For: You.

  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including nights and weekends
  • Team player, working effectively with peers and supervisors
  • Able to respond appropriately to changes in direction or unexpected situations
  • Knowledge of company standard software, systems, and procedures
  • Knowledge of merchandise flow in stores
  • Proven problem solving skills
  • Able to effectively coach, delegate, and follow-up on multiple people/tasks
  • Able to act quickly under challenging circumstances
  • Capable of multi-tasking
  • Superior communication and organizational skills with attention to detail
  • 1 year retail, 6 months leadership experience

Benefits include: Associate discount; EAP; smoking cessation; bereavement; 401(k) Associate contributions; child care & cell phone discounts; pet & legal insurance; credit union; referral bonuses. Those who meet service or hours requirements are also eligible for: 401(k) match; medical/dental/vision; HSA; health care FSA; life insurance; short/long term disability; paid parental leave; paid holidays/vacation/sick; auto/home insurance discounts; scholarship program; adoption assistance. All benefits are provided in accordance with and subject to the terms of the applicable plan or program and may change from time to time. Contact your TJX representative for more information.

In addition to our open door policy and supportive work environment, we also strive to provide a competitive salary and benefits package. TJX considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity and expression, marital or military status, or based on any individual's status in any group or class protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. TJX also provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable state and local law.

Applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment.

Address:

900 Dekalb Plaza Boulevard

Location:

USA Marshalls Store 1653 Fort Payne AL

This position has a starting pay range of USD $14.75 to $15.25 per hour. Actual starting pay is determined by a number of factors, including relevant skills, qualifications, and experience.

title: Final Documentation Specialist
description:
The Final Documentation Specialist will support the Documentation team by producing high‑quality data books, manuals that meet contractual specifications. This role involves gathering information from engineering, quality, ensuring compliance with company standards, and delivering documentation on time to support customer satisfaction and project success.

  • Create, compile, produce applicable documentation (i.e., Manufacturing Record Books (MRBs), Supplier MRBs, User Manuals (USMs), & Declaration of Conformities (DoCs)), review MRBs/USMs for accuracy, and provide correctional feedback as needed for U.S. Final Documentation Groups.

  • Utilize engineering document database system to create, compile and produce engineering USMs for customer equipment.

  • Communicate with internal departments and vendors to correct traceability and retrieve missing documentation to complete MRBs, Supplier MRBs, & USMs.

  • Transmit electronic USM & MRB copies and print hard copies when required per customer contract.

  • Provide basic training to new employees on department process, work instructions, & how to compile/review MRBs, Supplier MRBs, USMs, & DOCs.

  • Perform other work-related tasks as necessary, including the ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

  • Comply with all NOV Company and HSE policies and procedures.

    FACILITY/GROUP SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Generate equipment genealogy reports to confirm Build of Material (BOM) of component assemblies.

  • Review and assure manufacturing documentation is available, and traceability is verified before equipment can be shipped from facility.
  • Ensure the traceability from warehouse picklists of the Work Orders match the ERP system.
  • Keep accurate schedule of assigned orders for timely delivery to meet deadlines.
  • Transmit and communicates with Third Party companies for review and follow-up of our Manufacturing Records Books for certification per Customer Contract.

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • 0-2 plus years of manufacturing data books knowledge.

  • Minimum understanding of Engineering documents and build of material (BOM).

  • Minimun understanding and be able to read manufacturing work orders.
